title: Can I BEAT Petrified Chess?
summary: chess.com Petrified Chess: any non-pawn piece that makes a capture turns to stone where it lands and becomes a permanent immovable block; pawns are never petrified and can also step sideways. He discovers the sideways pawn rule mid-game, wins two games and draws the third by repetition (2.5/3).
rules: When a non-pawn piece captures, the capturing piece is petrified (turned to stone) on that square and can never move again; it acts as a blocking obstacle that cannot be captured.
Pawns are not petrified when they capture, so pawns are the only pieces that can capture freely (makes pawns 'overpowered').
Pawns may also move one square sideways (non-capturing) - an extra rule he discovered at ~6:15.
Kings: inferred kings cannot be petrified (king captures not discussed).
A points counter awards points for petrifications (shown in chess.com UI; he did not understand it).
